items.stem: A car tows a trailer with a light rigid tow-bar. Which statement about their accelerations is true?
options: the trailer has a smaller acceleration
the accelerations are in opposite directions
items.markingKey: They move together as one system.

items.stem: Explain why the tension in a tow-rope does not appear in the equation of motion for the whole car-and-trailer system.
items.answer: The tension acts on the car and on the trailer in opposite directions (an internal force), so the two cancel when the system is treated as a whole.
items.markingKey: B1 internal force; B1 equal and opposite forces cancel [2]

items.stem: A tractor of mass 1800 kg tows a cart of mass 400 kg along a level road with driving force 3000 N; resistances are 300 N on the tractor and 100 N on the cart. Tariq says the tension in the tow-bar equals the driving force, 3000 N. Explain the error and find the tension.
items.answer: The driving force accelerates both vehicles; for the cart alone T − 100 = 400a with a = 1.18 m s⁻², so T = 573 N.
items.markingKey: B1 considers the trailer alone; B1 correct tension [2]

items.stem: A lorry of mass 800 kg tows a trailer of mass 400 kg along a straight level road by means of a light rigid tow-bar. The driving force is 4000 N and the resistances to motion are 300 N on the lorry and 250 N on the trailer. Find the acceleration and the tension in the tow-bar.
items.markingKey: M1 whole system; A1 a; M1 trailer alone; A1 T [4]

items.stem: When a car towing a trailer brakes, what force may the tow-bar exert on the trailer?

items.stem: A tractor of mass 1500 kg tows a cart of mass 200 kg along a level road. The driving force is 2500 N and the resistances are 200 N on the tractor and 100 N on the cart. Find the tension in the tow-bar.
items.markingKey: For the cart: T − R₂ = ma.

items.stem: A locomotive of mass 1500 kg tows a truck of mass 600 kg along a level road with driving force 4000 N; resistances are 300 N on the locomotive and 100 N on the truck. Priya says the tension in the tow-bar equals the driving force, 4000 N. Explain the error and find the tension.
items.answer: The driving force accelerates both vehicles; for the truck alone T − 100 = 600a with a = 1.71 m s⁻², so T = 1130 N.
items.markingKey: B1 considers the trailer alone; B1 correct tension [2]

items.stem: A car of mass 1000 kg tows a trailer of mass 500 kg along a level road with driving force 4000 N; resistances are 500 N on the car and 100 N on the trailer. The car then brakes. Explain why the tow-bar may now be in thrust rather than tension.
items.answer: If the car decelerates more rapidly than resistance alone would decelerate the trailer, the bar must push back on the trailer to slow it: a thrust.
items.markingKey: B1 trailer would otherwise decelerate less; B1 bar pushes: thrust [2]

items.stem: Explain why the tension in the string over a pulley is less than the weight of the heavier particle but more than the weight of the lighter one.
items.answer: The heavier particle accelerates downwards, so its weight exceeds T; the lighter accelerates upwards, so T exceeds its weight.
items.markingKey: B1 heavier: mg > T; B1 lighter: T > mg [2]

items.stem: Explain the modelling assumptions made when particles of masses 8 kg and 5 kg hang over a smooth peg and the acceleration is found as 2.31 m s⁻².
items.answer: The string is light and inextensible (same tension, same acceleration magnitude), the peg is smooth (tension the same on both sides), the particles are point masses, and air resistance is ignored.
items.markingKey: B1 string assumptions; B1 smooth peg and particles [2]

items.stem: Particles of masses 8 kg and 3 kg hang over a smooth pulley. Zara says the tension in the string is 30 N, the weight of the lighter particle. Explain the error and find the tension.

items.stem: Explain why, after the heavier particle in a pulley system hits the ground, the lighter particle continues to rise.
items.answer: The string goes slack, so the lighter particle moves freely under gravity; it has upward velocity at that instant and decelerates at g until it stops.
